podcast.title: Richard Carpenter's Vision (1970)
podcast.body: After hearing Paul Williams's jingle for Crocker Citizens Bank, Richard Carpenter was profoundly convinced that "We've Only Just Begun" was a hit song. He specifically believed that his sister Karen Carpenter's unique vocals could bring the tune to life, leading to their iconic recording. "Richard Carpenter was convinced not only that the song was a hit, but that his sister, Karen Carpenter's vocals, could bring it to life."

podcast.title: Lester Bangs Concert Review (1971)
podcast.body: Rock critic Lester Bangs reviewed a Carpenters concert in 1971 and, predictably, did not enjoy the show, primarily due to the band's lack of stage presence and the laid-back attitude of the concert-goers, rather than the music itself. He did, however, appreciate their song "We've Only Just Begun." "The rock critic Lester Banges was given the task of reviewing a concert by the Carpenter's in 1971. The Carpenter's were the brother and sister duo Karen and Richard from White Suburbia in California."

podcast.title: Goodyear Tire Company Christmas Album (1972)
podcast.body: "Merry Christmas Darling" by The Carpenters appeared on Goodyear Tire Company's 1972 Christmas album, which primarily featured standard holiday songs, before it was included on a Carpenters' album. "Now, good your tire company used to pet out Christmas albums, and it was mostly standards, but this song was on their 1972 release."

podcast.title: White House Visit (1973)
podcast.body: The Carpenters visited President Richard Nixon at the White House in 1973, reinforcing their image as wholesome and good, an image that Richard Carpenter grew tired of. "It certainly didn't help that they visited Richard Nixon at the White House in 1973."

podcast.title: "Ice Cream" Body of Work
podcast.body: Lester Bangs, in his 1971 review, described the Carpenters' body of work as akin to "ice cream," characterizing it as "pleasant and mildly bracing." "And he described the body of work by Karen and Richard Carpenter as being like ice cream, quote pleasant and mildly bracing."

podcast.title: "White Middle Class American Kids" Identity
podcast.body: Richard Carpenter articulated the band's identity by stating, "we were white middle class American kids. We wrote like that, we sang like that, we dressed like that, we lived like that," in response to criticism that their music was boring. He emphasized that while they were pop, they were not "bland, unimaginative pop music." "Richard said of the Carpenter's, we were white middle class American kids. We wrote like that, we sang like that, we dressed like that, we lived like that."

podcast.title: Complaint Against Sex Pistols
podcast.body: As artists on A&M Records, The Carpenters complained about the label's decision to sign the Sex Pistols, contributing to the latter's rapid termination from the label. "And when other A&M artists like the Carpenters complained, the pistols were dropped."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Crocker National Bank Campaign Failure
podcast.body: The "We've Only Just Begun" jingle was created for a Crocker National Bank of California campaign aimed at young couples seeking loans. While the TV commercial featuring the jingle was popular, it did not achieve its desired effect as the many young people interested in loans lacked the necessary collateral. Consequently, Crocker suspended the campaign. "So the whole thing was a flop. And Crocker suspended the campaign."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Jingle Licensing to Recoup Costs
podcast.body: After Crocker National Bank suspended its campaign, the agency Hal Reiner and Partners, rather than taking a financial hit for the work done, attempted to recoup costs by licensing the "We've Only Just Begun" jingle to other banks. This move inadvertently led to Richard Carpenter discovering the song. "Rather than take the financial hit for all the work, writing and partners had done, they tried to recoup as much as they could by licensing the jingle to other banks."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Karen Carpenter's Drumming Prowess
podcast.body: Karen Carpenter displayed her drumming skills in a 1976 TV special, performing a drum solo across multiple kits with various percussion instruments. Despite the band's adult contemporary sound, she was an "awesome drummer" and considered herself primarily a drummer who happened to sing, rather than a singer who played drums. Her performance challenged perceptions of women playing drums at the time. "Karen believed that she was a drummer who just happened to sing."

podcast.title: Karen Carpenter's Voice
podcast.body: Karen Carpenter's vocal ability was consistently described as "perfect," with Melinda Newman, executive editor at Billboard, specifically praising her "pure sublime perfection" on "Merry Christmas Darling" for its conveyance of yearning, sadness, and hope. "Her vocal on Merry Christmas darling, as she longs for her loved one, who is a way for Christmas a New Year's Day, is pure sublime perfection. She conveys the perfect mix of yearning, sadness and hope, since she knows even though it's unspoken, they will be joyfully reunited after the holidays."

podcast.title: Late Scopatone Films
podcast.body: The Carpenters were among the artists who continued to make films for Scopatone machines even as their popularity declined after 1967. The last Scopatone film was made in 1978, highlighting the machine's prolonged but tapering existence. "The Carpenters and Abba made films for the machines."

podcast.title: New York Philharmonic Orchestra Performance
podcast.body: Karen Carpenter performed "Merry Christmas Darling" backed by the New York Philharmonic Orchestra during the Carpenters Christmas special in 1978. "She's being backed there by the New York Philharmonic Orchestra."

podcast.title: Richard Carpenter's Perfectionism
podcast.body: Richard Carpenter was known for his perfectionism in music production, exemplified by his meticulous effort to create a "technically perfect Christmas album" with "Christmas Portrait." This dedication to polish, while appreciated by many for its craftsmanship, sometimes alienated listeners who found the Carpenters' sound too refined. "I mean, who, who does that? Who sets out to make a technically perfect Christmas album? Well, he does because he's a perfectionist."

podcast.title: Richard Puler's Early Life and Connection to The Carpenters
podcast.body: Richard Puler wrote the lyrics for "Merry Christmas Darling" in 1944 when he was 18, as a Christmas gift for a girl he loved, though they broke up before he could give it to her. He had a recording made on a 78-rpm record but never remembered who sang it. Years later, in the late 1960s, Karen Carpenter's parents hired him to give her voice lessons, and Karen subsequently joined the Cal State Long Beach choir, which Puler directed, leading to his collaboration with the Carpenters. "In 1944, an 18-year-old named Richard Puler wrote the lyrics to Mary Christmas Darling for a girl he loved. He planned to give it to her as a Christmas present, but then they broke up."

podcast.title: Rolling Stone Ranking
podcast.body: Rolling Stone magazine's critics ranked "We've Only Just Begun" as the 414th entry among their prestigious list of "500 greatest songs of all time." This significant ranking highlights the song's lasting musical importance and cultural impact beyond its commercial genesis. "Their critics ranked Weve Only Just Begun 414th among their 500 greatest songs of all time."

podcast.title: Signature Hit Status
podcast.body: Both Richard Carpenter and critics from Rolling Stone magazine consistently regard "We've Only Just Begun" as The Carpenters' signature hit. This underscores the song's enduring legacy and critical acclaim, despite its origins as a commercial jingle. "And to this day, Richard Carpenter regards Weve Only Just Begun as the Carpenter's signature hit."

xref.title: A&M Records Deal and Termination (1977) - Six-Day Contract
xref.body: Two months after being dropped by EMI, A&M Records signed the Sex Pistols. However, a party immediately following the signing at the label's offices resulted in significant damage, and guitarist Steve Jones was reportedly "having sex with a staffer in the bathroom." Facing questions from head office in Los Angeles and complaints from other A&M artists like The Carpenters, the label dropped the Sex Pistols after just six days, providing a buyout worth £75,000. "They were on A&M for just six days."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Albert Hammond Jr.'s Background and Role
xref.body: Albert Hammond Jr. is the son of Albert Hammond Sr., a successful songwriter who wrote songs for artists like Celine Dion, Aretha Franklin, Whitney Houston, Willie Nelson, Chicago, and The Carpenters, and had a writing credit on Radiohead's "Creep." In the early days of The Strokes, Albert was the band's business guy, booking gigs and pitching record companies under the pseudonym "Paul Spencer" (from his fake ID). He collected rejection letters by posting them on a wall. Crucially, he had a credit card funded by his father, which paid for essential band expenses like guitar strings, cables, drumsticks, and rehearsal PA. "Albert was the business guy of the band in the early days. He was the guy who booked gigs and pitch record companies, usually under the pseudonym Paul Spencer, which was the name he used on his old fake ID."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Prolific Songwriter
xref.body: Albert Hammond Sr. is a successful songwriter who wrote numerous songs for a wide array of prominent artists. His credits include songs for Celine Dion, Aretha Franklin, Whitney Houston, Willie Nelson, Chicago, and The Carpenters. He also received a writing credit on Radiohead's song "Creep" due to its melodic resemblance to "The Air That I Breathe," a song he wrote for The Hollies in the 1970s, as determined by a court case. "He wrote this song. Dad also wrote songs for Celine Dion, where we at the Franklin Whitney Houston, Willie Nelson, Chicago, the Carpenter, and a ton of others."
